diagnostic_evidence.quote: \item Conjecture 1.2 holds for the special case $\sigma_{\rm opt}$ and $z\in V_\beta$, where $r_N(x)$ also achieves the fastest rate  among all $\sigma>0$.
Our analysis further reveals that the parameter choice $\sigma_{\rm opt}=\frac{\pi\sqrt{2(2-\beta)}}{\sqrt{\alpha}}$  achieves the fastest convergence rate among all $\sigma>0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims in the abstract ("explicitly derives the optimal pole clustering parameter"), the introduction, the bullet remarks after Theorem mainthm ("attains/achieves the fastest convergence rate among all \sigma>0"), the title of Section 4 ("the optimality of the parameter \sigma_{\rm opt}"), and the conclusions, that \sigma_{\rm opt} is the fastest choice among all \sigma>0. What is actually proved (Theorems mainthm, mainthm2, mainthmG, corner) is, for each fixed \sigma>0, the existence of one LP approximant whose error is bounded above by the stated rate; these proved upper bounds are optimized at \sigma_{\rm opt}. Upper bounds cannot show that other parameters converge more slowly: one must rule out cancellations in the Poisson/residue sums and in \bar E=\frac{\sin(\alpha\pi)}{(-1)^m\alpha\pi}(E_T+E_Q+E_{PA}), and the possibility that different coefficients with the same poles \eqref{eq:tapered2} and \sigma\ne\sigma_{\rm opt} also attain e^{-\pi\sqrt{2(2-\beta)N\alpha}}. No lower-bound argument appears anywhere in the source; the only support is the monotonicity of the proved upper bounds plus the numerical Fig. rateex. (Optimality among \sigma for \beta=0, 0<\alpha<1 is only imported from the cited [XYW2024]; the general-\alpha, general-\beta claim is the paper's own and is unsupported.)

failure_location.quote: represents the optimal choice among all candidates in \eqref{eq:tapered2} for achieving the fastest convergence rate

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either supply a lower-bound analysis showing that for \sigma\ne\sigma_{\rm opt} no LP with poles \eqref{eq:tapered2} can beat the corresponding stated rate (sharpness of the quadrature/residue estimates plus minimality over coefficient choices), or weaken every optimality statement to what is proved: the proved upper bound is maximized at \sigma_{\rm opt} and attains the conjectured optimal rate \mathcal{O}(e^{-\pi\sqrt{2(2-\beta)N\alpha}}) (Stahl-optimal when \beta=0).
issues.overall_effect: All "optimal pole clustering parameter" and "fastest among all \sigma>0" assertions (abstract, introduction, remarks after Theorem mainthm, Section 4 title, conclusions, and the parameter discussion around Theorem corner) exceed what the paper establishes. The formal convergence theorems themselves, including the confirmation of Conjectures 1.1 and 1.2 at \sigma=\sigma_{\rm opt}, are unaffected.
issues.title: Optimality of sigma_opt among all sigma asserted without any lower-bound argument
issues.why_classification: The weakest supported resolution keeps every formal result (the conjecture confirmations and the rate upper bounds are intact) but withdraws the substantive advertised guarantee that \sigma_{\rm opt} is the fastest/optimal parameter; the alternative repair requires a genuinely new nontrivial lower-bound argument. Not serious because a recognizably comparable set of claims survives with no change to the formal theorems; not minor because a substantive promise is lost or needs new analysis.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume $\Re(u_0(z))=T+\alpha\log{\frac{x}{C}}>\sqrt{h}+\alpha$, which is equivalent to the condition $x\in (x^*,1]$.

issues.failure_explanation: The suprema over S_beta in \eqref{eq:l1} and \eqref{eq:l2} are actually infinite for large T: for z=xe^{\pm i\theta\pi/2}\in S_\beta with x=Ce^{\frac1\alpha(\sqrt h-T)}\in(0,1], a pole u_j(z)=T+\alpha\log(x/C)+i\alpha\pi(2j-1\pm\theta/2) has real part exactly \sqrt h, i.e., there is t in the stated range with Ce^{\frac1\alpha(\sqrt h+it-T)}+z=0 (e.g., t=\alpha\pi(1+\theta/2)\in(0,2m_0\alpha\pi] for the + sign, since 1+\theta/2<2\le 2m_0; for \beta\ge1 also t=\alpha\pi(1-\theta/2)\in[0,\pi\alpha/2]). Such z lies in S_\beta\setminus S_\beta', so f^{(l,1)}(\sqrt h+it,z) is unbounded and the claimed \mathcal O(T^le^{-T}) sup-norm bounds fail. The bounds do hold for z\in S_\beta': there x>x^*=e\,Ce^{\frac1\alpha(\sqrt h-T)}, so by the reverse triangle inequality |Ce^{\frac1\alpha(\sqrt h+it-T)}+z|\ge x-Ce^{\frac1\alpha(\sqrt h-T)}\ge(1-e^{-1})x, and |Ce^{\frac1\alpha(\sqrt h+it-T)}+s_k|\ge s_k-Ce^{\frac1\alpha(\sqrt h-T)}\ge\delta/2 for large T, yielding the same \mathcal O(T^le^{-T}) form.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the norms in \eqref{eq:l1} and \eqref{eq:l2} to z\in S_\beta' (justified by the reverse-triangle lower bound using x>x^*); the remainder of the proof is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Two displayed estimates in the proof of Theorem eq:quaderrthm are false as written over the stated domain S_\beta. The proof of Theorem eq:quaderrthm, and hence Theorems mainthm, mainthm2, mainthmG and corner, are unaffected because Case 1 invokes these bounds only for z\in S_\beta', where they hold.
issues.title: Vertical-segment norm bounds \eqref{eq:l1}-\eqref{eq:l2} are false over the full sector S_beta
issues.why_classification: A short local repair (restricting the domain of two intermediate bounds to S_\beta', where they are readily verified) preserves the theorem's statement, the convergence rates, and every dependent result; no new lemma or replacement argument is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: With \hbar=h the even extension satisfies \bar f^{(l)}(0,z)=f^{(l)}(h,z)\ne0, hence h\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}\bar f^{(l)}(jh,z)=hf^{(l)}(h,z)+2r^{(l)}_{N_t}(z)+2h\sum_{j>N_t}f^{(l)}(jh,z). The identity in the second line of \eqref{eq:quaderror1} therefore omits the term -hf^{(l)}(h,z), and the final reverse-triangle inequality, which subtracts only |E_{fd}^{(l)}(z)| and the tail 2h\sum_{j>N_t}|f^{(l)}(jh,z)|, is not valid as written. The omitted term has the same order as the kept terms: by the paper's own estimate |f^{(l)}(h,z)|\le\frac{\mathbb T_{m,\beta}T^lC^\alpha e^{\sqrt h-T}}{2\sqrt h\,\delta^m{\cal X}(\beta)}, so h|f^{(l)}(h,z)|=\mathcal O(T^le^{-T}), and reinstating it yields the same final bound for |E_Q^{(l)}(z)|.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the term -hf^{(l)}(h,z) to the identity in \eqref{eq:quaderror1} and subtract h|f^{(l)}(h,z)|=\mathcal O(T^le^{-T}) in the following inequality; no other change is needed.
issues.overall_effect: One identity/inequality link in the proof of Theorem eq:quaderrthm is invalid as written; the quadrature-error estimate \eqref{errquad0} and all downstream theorems survive once the term is included.
issues.title: Missing hf^{(l)}(h,z) term in the Case-1 Poisson-sum identity \eqref{eq:quaderror1}
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short local algebraic correction whose additional term has the same order as terms already estimated in the paper; every claim, rate, and guarantee is preserved without any new argument.

issues.failure_explanation: In Case 2, \lambda_0=\lceil(\sigma+2)/\sigma\rceil^2>1, so the constant middle value f^{(l)}(h,z) does not equal f^{(l)}(\lambda_0h,z): \bar f^{(l)} has jump discontinuities at u=\pm\lambda_0h, which are grid points of the Poisson sum. The symmetric-average hypothesis w(u)=\lim_{t\to0^+}\frac{w(u-t)+w(u+t)}2 of the invoked Stenger theorem therefore fails at these points, and the definition contradicts the later identity \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty}\bar f^{(l)}(u,z)du=2\lambda_0hf^{(l)}(\lambda_0h,z)+\ldots, which uses the value f^{(l)}(\lambda_0h,z). Taking the middle value to be f^{(l)}(\lambda_0h,z) makes the extension continuous, restores the theorem's hypotheses, and agrees with the later display.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the middle-branch value f^{(l)}(h,z) by f^{(l)}(\lambda_0h,z) in \eqref{eq:extension_of_fnew} (alternatively keep the definition and add a point-value correction of order \mathcal O(T^le^{-T}) to both the Poisson sum and the integral evaluation).
issues.overall_effect: As constructed, the Case-2 extension does not satisfy the hypotheses of the Poisson summation theorem being invoked, and the paper is internally inconsistent about the extension's value on [-\lambda_0h,\lambda_0h]; the final Case-2 estimate is unaffected because the discrepancy is a single grid-point value of order \mathcal O(T^le^{-T}).
issues.title: Case-2 extension \eqref{eq:extension_of_fnew} is discontinuous and inconsistent with its later use
issues.why_classification: A one-symbol local repair (or a same-order point-value correction) makes the construction continuous, internally consistent, and within the invoked theorem's hypotheses; the method, the rates, and all conclusions are preserved.

issues.failure_explanation: The last equality in \eqref{Poissonsum2} claims that \frac{1}{e^{\frac{4\pi^2\alpha}{h}(T+\alpha\log(\delta/C))}-1} is absorbed into \mathcal O(T^le^{-T}). Since \frac{4\pi^2\alpha}{h}=\frac{2}{2-\beta}\eta^2 with \eta=\sigma_{\rm opt}/\sigma, for \sigma>\sigma_{\rm opt} with \frac{2}{2-\beta}\eta^2<1 (e.g., \beta=1/2, \eta^2=0.3) this term has order e^{-\frac{2}{2-\beta}\eta^2T}, which decays strictly more slowly than e^{-T}, so the displayed equality is false in that regime. The Case-2 conclusion of Theorem eq:quaderrthm nevertheless follows from the preceding (valid) middle bound: for \sigma\le\sigma_{\rm opt} one has \frac{2}{2-\beta}\eta^2\ge1 and the sum is \mathcal O(T^le^{-T}); for \sigma>\sigma_{\rm opt} it is \mathcal O(T^le^{-T}+e^{-\frac{2}{2-\beta}\eta^2T})=\mathcal O(e^{-\eta^2T}), matching \eqref{errquad0}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep the middle bound and split the two regimes: state the Poisson sum as \mathcal O(T^le^{-T}) for \sigma\le\sigma_{\rm opt} and as \mathcal O(e^{-\eta^2T}) for \sigma>\sigma_{\rm opt}, instead of the single equality to \mathcal O(T^le^{-T}).
issues.overall_effect: One displayed asymptotic equality in the Case-2 analysis is invalid in part of the parameter range; Theorem eq:quaderrthm's statement and all dependent results are preserved by the correct two-regime reading.
issues.title: Final equality of \eqref{Poissonsum2} fails for sigma>sigma_opt with small eta
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short local restatement of one intermediate display into the two regimes already used throughout the paper; the theorem's statement, rates, and all dependent results are preserved with no new argument.
